author: GamingBolt
description:
Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced might have just made its open world so seamless, it transformed the original Black Flag into a title that could now be a benchmark for how future titles in the genre approach side content. 

It’s a system that seems so simple in its design, but quite complex in its execution as it created a complex web of economic growth, character progression, and base building that’s woven in quite seamlessly into a pirate/Assassin fantasy that already works very well. 

Doing so has made it feels like a modernization of a gameplay loop that was only limited by the hardware it was released into, but has now been refined and polished into a potent mix of mechanical prowess and narrative quality. Join us as we take a look at how the fantasy feeds itself in this one, and how we’re the ones eating well in the process.
title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced Shows Modern Open World Games How Side Content Should Be Done

author: GamingBolt
description:
College Football 27 has been in the news for a lot of the wrong reasons, despite bringing some very good ones to be in the spotlight for. Of course, monetising single-player gameplay modes was never going to go down well with its players, and many of you came together to get EA to take back a rather sneaky effort to further monetize a franchise that’s been quite valuable over the last couple of years.

But is this victory complete yet, or is it perhaps the first step on the road to real glory achieved through meaningful change? That’s what we’re looking to answer as we look to the franchise's future, and address a rather worrisome interpretation of what EA might be taking away from this entire fiasco.
title: College Football 27 Players Forced EA to Listen, But College Football 28 Is the Real Test

author: GamingBolt
description:
It's funny how time flies – over two years ago, Palworld was the hottest game on the market, despite launching in early access and having numerous issues. Call it the desire for an expansive 3D creature-collecting title after constant disappointment with Pokemon, but there was something intangible about Pocketpair's formula of survival crafting and open-world exploration. 

So much so that it sold two million copies in its first 24 hours, eventually crossed 2.1 million concurrent players on Steam alone, and within a month, hit 25 million players with Xbox included. In that time, it truly felt like a Pal's world, and we were all just living in it...with the odd human captive or three in tow. In an environment where live-service games not named Helldivers 2 were crashing left and right, and the triple-A industry suddenly going on about quadruple-A, it was a breath of fresh air.
title: Palworld 1.0 - Why Are MILLIONS of Gamers Addicted?
